## A — Authority and uncertainty
This dossier studies the selected Sharing the road pages. It preserves the accepted source snapshot while keeping its assessment debt visible. The official question count, passing standard, format and test duration remain unknown; a practice mastery threshold must never be described as an official passing score. Source revision frequency and currentness have not been established (verify AK-STABILITY). Examination policy remains nullable (verify AK-EXAM).

sections.heading: B — Sharing the road
sections.markdown:
## B — Audience and scope
The audience is an Alaska first-time passenger-car applicant studying sharing the road. Use the exact selected source pages, plain definitions, complete qualifiers and the distinction between a source snapshot and a current official rule. Commercial operation and road-test maneuver grading remain outside this written-study scope.

sections.heading: C — Sharing the road
sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing and examination knowledge
FACT_ID: sec09-F001 | anchor: P48
People walking, bicycling, working on foot near traffic or using mobility devices are vulnerable because a motor vehicle offers them no crash protection.

FACT_ID: sec09-F002 | anchor: P48
Higher collision speeds greatly reduce a pedestrian's chance of surviving a passenger-car impact.

FACT_ID: sec09-F003 | anchor: P48
Look for pedestrians and bicyclists at all times, using extra care at dusk, dawn, night and in bad weather.

FACT_ID: sec09-F004 | anchor: P48
Slow and prepare to stop before turning into or entering a crosswalk.

FACT_ID: sec09-F005 | anchor: P48
Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and seek eye contact.

FACT_ID: sec09-F006 | anchor: P48
Stop far enough behind a crosswalk that drivers in other vehicles can see crossing pedestrians.

FACT_ID: sec09-F007 | anchor: P48
Obey a stop sign where a separated pathway crosses a road entrance.

FACT_ID: sec09-F008 | anchor: P48
Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk because it may hide a person crossing.

FACT_ID: sec09-F009 | anchor: P48
Pay particular attention to speed limits near people in the street, schools and neighborhoods with children.

FACT_ID: sec09-F010 | anchor: P48
Check carefully for pedestrians before backing.

FACT_ID: sec09-F011 | anchor: P49
Pedestrians should use crosswalks, obey traffic controls and watch for turning vehicles before crossing.

FACT_ID: sec09-F012 | anchor: P49
A pedestrian should not begin crossing on a nearly expired green signal or a steady or flashing don't-walk indication.

FACT_ID: sec09-F013 | anchor: P49
When walking along a highway, use the left side facing approaching vehicles.

FACT_ID: sec09-F014 | anchor: P49
The handbook prohibits soliciting rides or being intoxicated on or along a highway.

FACT_ID: sec09-F015 | anchor: P49
Light-colored clothing makes a pedestrian easier to see beside a road at night.

FACT_ID: sec09-F016 | anchor: P49
Bicyclists have the right to share the road and travel in the same direction as motor vehicles.

FACT_ID: sec09-F017 | anchor: P49
Before turning, parallel parking, opening a door or leaving a curb, turn your head to check blind spots for bicyclists rather than relying only on mirrors.

FACT_ID: sec09-F018 | anchor: P49
Apply right-of-way rules to bicyclists just as to other vehicles.

FACT_ID: sec09-F019 | anchor: P49
Use extra care near young bicyclists; the manual cautions that children younger than nine lack the development needed to handle complex traffic safely.

FACT_ID: sec09-F020 | anchor: P50
Bicyclists must obey traffic signs, signals and other traffic laws, although Alaska does not assess license points for bicycle traffic violations.

FACT_ID: sec09-F021 | anchor: P50
Bicycle safety guidance recommends wearing a helmet, riding near the road's right edge and not carrying another person on the bicycle.

FACT_ID: sec09-F022 | anchor: P50
A bicyclist should signal turns, lane changes and stops by hand.

FACT_ID: sec09-F023 | anchor: P50
A bicyclist signals left by extending the left arm straight to the left and signals stopping by bending the extended left arm downward at the elbow.

FACT_ID: sec09-F024 | anchor: P50
A bicyclist may signal a right turn with the right arm straight to the right or the left arm extended and bent upward at the elbow.

FACT_ID: sec09-F025 | anchor: P50
Bicyclists should watch cars at driveways, cross streets and parking places and avoid swerving when checking behind.

FACT_ID: sec09-F026 | anchor: P50
Bicyclists must yield to pedestrians and keep their bicycles in good condition.

FACT_ID: sec09-F027 | anchor: P50
Stay out of motor-vehicle blind spots and do not pass a turning vehicle on the side toward which it is turning.

FACT_ID: sec09-F028 | anchor: P50
Before crossing in front of a driver, make eye contact even when you have priority.

FACT_ID: sec09-F029 | anchor: P50
The manual advises bicyclists using headphones to leave one earbud out so they can hear surrounding hazards.

FACT_ID: sec09-F030 | anchor: P51
Motorcyclists have the same roadway rights and responsibilities as other drivers.

FACT_ID: sec09-F031 | anchor: P51
A motorcycle's distance and speed can be difficult for another driver to judge, so consciously look for motorcycles.

FACT_ID: sec09-F032 | anchor: P51
Before turning left across an oncoming motorcycle's path, look again and make sure its position and speed are understood.

Misconceptions: Treat closely related requirements as separate rules; preserve the triggering condition and any exception given in each fact [P48].
Mnemonics: Remember the condition together with the required action; this is an authored study cue.
Glossary: Definitions in the fact blocks keep the source context rather than substituting a broader rule.
Dynamic isolation: Source thresholds remain snapshot-specific until current official reconciliation.

sections.heading: C2 — Sharing the road
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Licensing and examination knowledge
FACT_ID: sec09-F033 | anchor: P52
Do not assume a motorcycle's blinking turn signal means it will turn, because many motorcycle indicators do not cancel automatically.

FACT_ID: sec09-F034 | anchor: P52
Allow a motorcycle the same recommended four-second following gap as other vehicles.

FACT_ID: sec09-F035 | anchor: P52
Motorcycles need the full lane; do not move into the lane beside a motorcycle even if it is traveling near one edge.

FACT_ID: sec09-F036 | anchor: P52
A rider may change position within a lane to improve visibility or avoid an obstacle.

FACT_ID: sec09-F037 | anchor: P52
Increase the following gap behind a motorcycle on a wet or slippery road and account for glare, especially at night.

FACT_ID: sec09-F038 | anchor: P52
Crosswinds and the wind blast from large trucks may push a motorcycle sideways, particularly on open highways and bridges.

FACT_ID: sec09-F039 | anchor: P52
Gravel, debris, pavement seams, rain grooves, small animals or manhole covers may cause a rider to change speed or direction.

FACT_ID: sec09-F040 | anchor: P52
A motorcyclist approaching railroad tracks may slow down, rise off the seat or change angle to cross the tracks more directly.

FACT_ID: sec09-F041 | anchor: P52
On metal or grated bridges, a rider may slow and move toward the lane center or react suddenly to wobbling, so be prepared.

FACT_ID: sec09-F042 | anchor: P53
When approaching a stopped school bus from behind with flashing red lights, stop before reaching it and do not pass.

FACT_ID: sec09-F043 | anchor: P53
A driver behind the school bus must remain stopped until its stop sign retracts, red lights end and the bus moves again, or the bus driver signals permission to proceed.

FACT_ID: sec09-F044 | anchor: P53
When meeting a school bus with flashing amber lights, slow down and stop when the bus stops, its red lights flash and its stop sign extends.

FACT_ID: sec09-F045 | anchor: P53
A driver meeting the stopped bus must wait for its stop sign to retract and red lights to end before proceeding cautiously.

FACT_ID: sec09-F046 | anchor: P53
On separated roadways with at least two lanes in each direction, a driver approaching a school bus going the opposite way need not stop for its displayed stop arm and red lights.

FACT_ID: sec09-F047 | anchor: P54
The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is required on vehicles traveling at 25 miles per hour or less.

FACT_ID: sec09-F048 | anchor: P54
By day, the slow-moving-vehicle emblem's solid fluorescent orange triangle attracts attention from approaching drivers.

FACT_ID: sec09-F049 | anchor: P54
At night, the emblem's reflective red triangular border identifies the slow-moving vehicle in headlights.

Handoff hints: Group the cited facts by their actual subject and condition. Use prerequisite relations only where one stated definition is needed to understand another fact.
